issue.title: `#[kani::stub]` on contracted functions

labels.name: [C] Bug
labels.description: This is a bug. Something isn't working.

comments.body: It would help to clarify whether stubbing a contracted target is intended to bypass the target contract entirely or require the replacement to satisfy it. A regression matrix should cover `ensures`, `requires`, and recursion contracts independently, because the missing `__kani_recursion_check_*` closure may be generated only for one contract-lowering path.
comments.body_html: It would help to clarify whether stubbing a contracted target is intended to bypass the target contract entirely or require the replacement to satisfy it. A regression matrix should cover ensures, requires, and recursion contracts independently, because the missing __kani_recursion_check_* closure may be generated only for one contract-lowering path.

comments.body:
Thanks, @hiSandog! I think this currently reflects a tooling limitation rather than intended semantics. With `#[kani::stub(abs_val, stub_abs_val)]`, the `abs_val` body should be fully abstracted away for that harness, so requiring contract-generated closure symbols from `abs_val` (e.g. `__kani_recursion_check_abs_val`) appears inconsistent.

In other words, stubbing and contract instrumentation are not composed correctly yet: the pipeline still resolves contract artifacts for the original target even when the call is redirected. I believe expected behavior is that plain stub works regardless of whether the target has `#[kani::ensures]` (unless we explicitly document otherwise).

*[Note to self]* Proposed fix direction: adjust ordering/resolution so contract closure lookup is skipped or redirected when a stub replacement is active, and add this reproducer as a regression test.
